reference_role: Only approved Enemy 1021 identity and Idle anchor. No previous HitRight image and no Enemy 1011 image uploaded.
prompt:
Edit the provided Enemy 1021 shield-soldier game character image into one single peak pose for an off-shield-side hit reaction. This is not an environment illustration, a video, or a multi-panel storyboard. The supplied image is the sole authority for character identity and art style. Preserve the exact same character, helmet, faceplate, red headcloth, cool gray armor, wooden shield, belt, boots, proportions, pixel density, lighting, palette, canvas, and front-facing camera.
    
    CAUSE OF THE ACTION: The soldier receives one sudden invisible blunt impact from off-screen at the RIGHT edge of the image, striking the exposed screen-right shoulder and upper screen-right chest that are not protected by the shield. The force travels from screen-right toward screen-left. The pose must clearly communicate: the attack came from the unshielded side and the shield failed to block it. This is not a block, a voluntary turn, an attack wind-up, or a chosen combat pose.
    
    BODY PEAK: The screen-right impact shoulder is visibly driven DOWN and slightly BACK. The screen-left shoulder is kicked UP by inertia, creating a strong asymmetric shoulder line. The chest and upper body recoil toward screen-left and slightly backward around a mostly fixed pelvis. The chest opens and lifts slightly. Do not fold forward, duck, curl inward, or topple the whole body sideways. The legs absorb the force with only slight weight-bearing flexion, while both boots remain fixed on their original ground contacts.
    
    HEAD IS A PRIMARY READ: The chest and shoulders react first, then the head follows with a short delay. The helmet and head are clearly knocked and tilted toward screen-left, with a slight backward whip. Create a strong visible side angle between the head and the chest so the head reads as thrown off balance by the impact. Lift the chin slightly and compress the neck into the shoulders. Keep the faceplate and glowing eye slit recognizable, but do not keep the head upright. Do not make it a calm glance toward screen-left, and do not turn it into a full profile. The head tilt should be close to a clear impact peak, not a barely visible turn.
    
    SHIELD IS THE SECOND PRIMARY READ: The shield remains held by the original shield hand on the screen-left side, but the impact pulls the shield-bearing arm toward screen-left and slightly opens the shield outward. Create a clearly visible gap between the shield's inner edge and the chest, exposing the screen-right upper chest, impact shoulder, and part of the torso. The shield must no longer sit flat across the front of the chest and must not form a complete defensive wall. It should visibly read as an open shield that failed to intercept the hit from the opposite side. Preserve the same shield, the same hand, and the same side. The shield must not change hands or sides, be released, fly away, spin away, break, or disappear. The shield-bearing forearm may become partially visible as it is passively pulled open, but it must not actively reset into a guarding pose.
    
    The empty screen-right arm trails passively with a relaxed elbow; the wrist and fingers hang or drag slightly outward. It must not deliberately guard the chest, attack, or pose. The red headcloth and ribbon follow the head and upper body with a short delayed response. They must remain attached to the character and must not fly above the helmet.
    
    Keep the pelvis center, belt buckle, root position, both boot contact points, and overall drawing scale stable. Only local chest, shoulders, head, shield arm, and shield articulation may change the silhouette. Do not use whole-character translation, scaling, inflation, squash, stretch, or camera movement to create the impact. Keep the character generally front-readable; a local torso reaction is allowed, but do not turn the whole body into a three-quarter view or profile, and never mirror the image.
    
    Preserve the fixed 1024x1024 canvas, locked orthographic front-facing camera, and flat light-gray background. Keep the helmet, shield, both arms, legs, and boots fully inside the canvas with ample empty margin. Continue the crisp stepped pixel contours, clustered block shading, hard cool-metal highlights, crimson cloth, brown leather, wooden shield boards, and dark iron fittings. Do not redesign the character or change the shield shape, equipment count, materials, or colors.
    
    DO NOT create a blocking pose, a shield pressed flat against the chest, a shield that fully hides the impact shoulder, or a completely motionless shield. Do not add an attacker, entering weapon, sparks, flashes, blood, dust, smoke, debris, speed lines, shockwaves, afterimages, or any other effect; a second hit; an intentional attack, shield raise, stepping, sliding, hopping, kneeling, falling, launching, or death; a shield swap, side switch, release, flight, break, or disappearance; an upright unmoving head, calm glance, downward curl, or full profile; whole-character translation, scaling, rotation, camera movement, three-quarter view, profile view, image mirroring, face repainting, changed helmet, armor, boots, limb count, background, canvas, text, UI, watermark, or extra character.
